issues.translation_quote: I was going to buy my wife a fur coat.
issues.justification: Minor shift, but more importantly the following lines lose the joke; see other items. (Low impact.)

issues.translation_quote: Senior economist at "Giprorybа", the Fisheries Design Institute.
issues.justification: Explanatory gloss inserted into spoken dialogue, and the name contains a Cyrillic 'а' typo. Unnatural for a subtitle.

issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, the fish street, - The "Chikanuk" pharmacy...
issues.justification: The mangled 'рыбна улица' (comic mispronunciation/ rehearsal of the fake foreign address) is rendered flatly; the humour of the gangster rehearsing is lost.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!"
issues.translation_quote: fall down, swear... Damn it! Oops, sorry, "Devil take it!"
issues.justification: The password joke hinges on the exact phrase 'Чёрт побери'; 'Damn it' vs 'Devil take it' is fine, but the phrase 'Devil take it' is archaic and then spelled inconsistently ('Dyevil take eet') in ways that don't reflect the foreign-accent gag consistently; also 'Damn it' is not an oath variant that needs correcting, so the gag is muddled.

issues.source_quote: Кемедэн райн, джёс сви ми Михаил Светлов? [А он точно с теплохода «Михаил Светлов»?]
issues.translation_quote: Is he definitely from the ship "Mikhail Svetlov"?
issues.justification: Fine in meaning, but the 'Mikhail Svetloff' mispronunciation pun with 'Светлофф' is lost partially. Minor impact.

issues.translation_quote: That's not topical!
issues.justification: Soviet-bureaucratic register ('не актуально') is flattened; 'topical' is off for a joking dismissal of the hare song.

issues.translation_quote: Carefool...
issues.justification: Odd invented pun not present in the source; the source is a mock-foreign/comic ending, and 'Carefool' misrepresents the effect.

issues.source_quote: Не положено, инструкция! Не взял попутных - это не таксист! Бандит!
issues.translation_quote: He wouldn't pick up passengers - he's no taxi driver! A bandit!
issues.justification: The 'попутных' (fares along the way) logic is slightly unclear; also 'let's give them a lift' for 'возьмём' loses the sense of Gorbunkov's suspicion.

issues.source_quote: Они будут следить за Вами, а мы - за ними.
issues.translation_quote: They'll be watching you, and we'll be watching them.
issues.justification: Fine. (No issue.)

issues.source_quote: Ничего, живите как жили, сами клюнут.
issues.translation_quote: Nothing, live as you used to, they'll take the bait.
issues.justification: Acceptable; the fishing metaphor then continues with 'живца', handled adequately.

issues.translation_quote: Mee-ow! You should be killed for this!
issues.justification: Nadya/ Lyolik's lines are mixed; the line is said by Lyolik to Gesha ('this deserves killing'), not addressed as 'you should be killed'—direction of the threat is changed.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках! Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: I hope you drop dead! I hope I see you in a coffin, in white slippers! I hope you have to live on one salary!
issues.justification: The neighbour's Yiddish/Odessan-flavoured dialect ('у гробу, у белых тапках') is rendered in standard English, losing the characteristic ethnic voice and comedy.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: A dog is man's best friend! ... the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: Adequate, but 'Управдом - друг человека' loses the bureaucratic-title punch; minor.

issues.source_quote: Поскользнулся, упал... Закрытый перелом... Потерял сознание, очнулся - гипс.
issues.translation_quote: I slipped, fell... closed fracture... Lost consciousness, came to - a cast!
issues.justification: The famous catchphrase is reproduced acceptably; but the later 'открытый перелом' gag (Nadya) is rendered 'open fracture' correctly. No issue.

issues.translation_quote: Treason!
issues.justification: In context 'измена' means marital infidelity (Nadya suspects adultery), not treason; the translation misreads and the later 'Как ты могла подумать такое' joke is distorted. Should be 'Infidelity!'.

issues.source_quote: Нет, мне надо посоветоваться с шефом! С начальством...
issues.translation_quote: No, I have to consult the boss! My superiors...
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.translation_quote: is located a toilette, type: lavatory
issues.justification: The comic bureaucratic-vulgar register is rendered with awkward 'toilette'; 'type: lavatory' is stilted and the joke of mixing high/low is weak.

issues.translation_quote: Due north, about... 50 meters away
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Who buys a pack of tickets, gets... A water tower!
issues.justification: The rhyme (пачку/водокачку) of the lottery jingle is lost; the humour of the doggerel doesn't carry.

issues.translation_quote: New rubles?
issues.justification: Reference to the 1961 currency reform is not explained; 'New rubles?' is confusing for English viewers, though terse.

issues.translation_quote: just in case of fire
issues.justification: Literal rendering of idiom; 'just in case' / 'just in case of emergency' is more natural, though the repeated gag is partly preserved.

issues.translation_quote: Fedenka... and it'd be nice to have... game bird.
issues.justification: 'Дичь' is also slang for the victim/target, and the 'game bird' rendering is stiff; the double meaning is not signalled, though repeated usage is consistent.

issues.translation_quote: Coo-coo...
issues.justification: 'Ку-ку' here is a drinking gesture/sound; 'Coo-coo' is a bird noise and may seem odd.

issues.source_quote: Вы к кому? К тебе! Но? Не узнаёшь?
issues.translation_quote: Who are you here for? For you! Oh? Don't you recognize me?
issues.justification: Speaker attribution muddled; 'Но?' is a colloquial 'Eh?', rendered 'Oh?'. Minor.

issues.translation_quote: War on drunkenness!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: Only two kinds drink champagne in the morning: aristocrats and degenerates!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: It's not my fault! He came by himself!
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Лопух... Такого возьмём без шума и пыли!
issues.translation_quote: A sucker... We'll take a guy like that with no noise and no dust!
issues.justification: 'Без шума и пыли' is a set phrase meaning 'quietly and cleanly'; 'no noise and no dust' is overly literal, though used consistently as a catchphrase.

issues.source_quote: Куй железо, не отходя от кассы!
issues.translation_quote: strike while the iron's hot, right at the cash register!
issues.justification: The malapropism blending two proverbs is preserved, which works.

issues.translation_quote: Kozlodoev... Kozadoev! Kozlodoev!
issues.justification: The wordplay is on the boss's repeated mangling of the name: 'Козлодоев' (goat-milker) vs 'Козадоев'. The third variant 'Казладоев' is flattened into the same 'Kozlodoev', so the gag is lost.

issues.translation_quote: Russo turisto... Obliko morale... verstehen?
issues.justification: Fine; these are deliberate mock-foreign and are preserved.

issues.source_quote: Мы вообще дальше Дубровки никуда не ездили.
issues.translation_quote: We've never been further than Dubrovka.
issues.justification: 'Dubrovka' is unexplained and the joke about provincial limits is slightly weakened; acceptable.

issues.translation_quote: Well then, let's begin, shall we!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Эти кретины уверяли, что он был без сознания...
issues.translation_quote: Those cretins swore he was unconscious...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, нет такого мужа, который, хоть на час бы не мечтал стать холостяком!
issues.translation_quote: there's no husband who hasn't dreamed of being a bachelor, if only for an hour!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Why'd you shave off your mustache?
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Lootenant. Senior one, I am...
issues.justification: The Yoda-like 'Senior one, I am' is an unmotivated stylization of 'Старшой я' and sounds odd.

issues.translation_quote: Ev'rything just like we agreed.
issues.justification: Dialect marker rendered inconsistently ('Ahlways', 'Ahll') with no clear pattern, reading as random misspellings rather than a voice.

issues.translation_quote: we'll ahll do time!
issues.justification: Ending gag: 'сядем усе' (we'll all go to prison) with the dialect; 'ahll' is distracting but meaning kept. Acceptable but the odd spelling is unnatural.

issues.translation_quote: Oh, I have to call my mommy...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: your husband is secretly visiting a mistress
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Well, if you're ever in Kolyma...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Let us pray to the Lord...
issues.justification: Church Slavonic archaic register is rendered in plain modern English for the liturgical lines ('Holy art Thou' is mixed), inconsistent.
